According to Smith et al. (2023), the prevalence of AI-generated text has increased significantly in academic settings. This finding aligns with earlier research by Johnson and Williams (2021), who predicted a 300 percent increase in automated content production by 2025.

Several frameworks have been proposed for detection. The GLTR tool (Gehrmann et al., 2019) uses statistical analysis of token probabilities. DetectGPT (Mitchell et al., 2023) employs perturbation-based methods. See also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10416 and https://openai.com/research/ai-text-classifier.

References:
1. Smith, J., Lee, K., and Patel, R. (2023). Prevalence of AI Text in Academic Submissions. Journal of Educational Technology, 45(2), 112-128.
2. Johnson, M. and Williams, S. (2021). Forecasting Automated Content Production. Digital Communications Quarterly, 18(4), 67-82.
3. Gehrmann, S., Strobelt, H., and Rush, A.M. (2019). GLTR: Statistical Detection and Visualization of Generated Text. ACL 2019.
